description: [S7.7, kind `scope`] A host dispatch made only of focus-child keys (RootHandler 12 / 13, no root-handler command) cannot be recorded: parse_trace (tick.cpp, KEYS THE WINDOW TREE'S FOCUS CHILD TOOK) gives such keys to the batch a HANDLER record opens, the open one or the next one of the same frame, and drops them at a FRAME record. The live core applies the batch and counts a violation ("a dispatch of focus keys only"), so that session's replay can differ from it. The trace host never gives one (all 70 equivalence rows 0 violations) and neither do the scripts (bio_type's four batches each hold a root handler). The app gives none either, because its focus callback answers 0 (U-1650). Real typing in the bio box sends KEYDOWN + WM_CHAR (focus 12 / 13) and then KEYUP (root handler 9), so it would make such a dispatch whenever the app splits a key's messages over two dispatches (U-1653).
path to resolution: When the app answers the focus callback from the port's focus state (U-1650): have the core hold a focus-only batch and give it, ahead of its commands, with the next dispatch that holds a root handler (live and replay then apply it at the same call), or keep a key's KEYDOWN / WM_CHAR / KEYUP in one dispatch.

description: [S7.7, kind `merge`] Two sections use the same Win32 runner op numbers. S7.1's live run used runner32 op 28, and S3.2's uncommitted runner32.cpp in the shared tree uses ops 28..32 (LiveTerrain attach / detach / object / log / snapshot). Both also edit the `default: // handle ops 17..27` comment line, so 1_capi.patch did not apply to the shared tree. 7_capi.patch moves the live run to op 40 (live.py OP_LIVE), inserts its block before `op == 20` and leaves that comment line alone. The patch now applies to HEAD and to the shared tree (7_make_patches.py).
path to resolution: Whoever merges S3 and S7 keeps the numbers distinct. A shared op table in runner32.cpp would prevent the next clash.

description: [S7.7, kind `method`] The bio_type session is a PREFIX session (live.cpp PrefixHost, sg_live_run_builtin kind 3). cov_r_bio's corpus trace answers up to its first dispatch holding a focus key. From that pump call the script answers: the trace's batch there is dropped, and the script's clock continues from the trace's last value, cursor and GetAsyncKeyState answers. The PREFIX part repeats the corpus path, and the script part is port-only input with no original run to compare. The gate compares the live run with its own replay (sg_run_boot), not with the original. A script alone did not reach the editor: from the sandbox's people palette, (272, 560) opens showHireEmployeeDialog (SG_TICK_TRACE), and mood5.sve's people palette shows clickEmployeeView.
path to resolution: S7.4's cross-check (an app recording replayed into the original) is where port-only input meets the original.

description: [S7.7, kind `method`] The script host answers an idle_ok call with an empty queue as "the player acts now". It skips a running wait step, and when the script has run out it stops the session (S7.6 rule). The character editor's release wait has a second pumpMessages (chareditor.cpp, `do pump_release while button`). That call is idle_ok, and without an `idle 1` after the check-mark click the session stopped inside the editor (579 records, editor never left, control 8 blind). With `idle 1` the session leaves the editor and control 8 reads RED at record 579 (g_golferTypes). The same pattern appears wherever a modal loop pumps after its last scripted input.
path to resolution: A script step that waits until the session's frame loop is back (`wait_body` exists; `wait_frames` is skipped by the act rule) could replace `idle N` there.

description: [S7.7, kind `coverage`] Two dispatches at Load pumps of one world load: the corpus has one (cov_r_flic_input). load_input gives two, 'z' and then 'x', each at the first Load call the core lets deliver. Between them the recorder writes a waitTicks-site clock record (separator(false)) after the first dispatch's palette QPC record, so the second batch's class is modal and parse_trace marks it `load`. The round trip PASSES with load_dispatches 2 (x64, and the Win32 run is identical, test_roundtrip_backends_identical). With the marker left out (control 7) it is RED at record 1 (g_zoomScale, g_cachedCameraTileX).
